articles.title: ISRO Successfully Tests CE20 Cryogenic Engine at Uprated 220 KN Thrust, Boosts LVM3 ...
articles.content: Updated 10 September 2026 at 13:21 IST The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) conducted a successful flight acceptance hot test of the CE20 cryogenic engine at an upgraded thrust of 220 kN on September 9, enhancing the LVM3 launch vehicle's payload capability and supporting the Gaganyaan programme. Asian News International India News 3 min read Follow : ISRO Successfully Tests CE20 Cryogenic Engine at Uprated 220 KN Thrust | Image: ISRO New Delhi: The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) successfully conducted a flight acceptance hot test of its CE20 cryogenic engine at uprated thrust conditions of 220 kN, advancing efforts to enhance the payload capability of the LVM3 launch vehicle and supporting the Gaganyaan programme. The test was conducted on September 9 at the ISRO Propulsion Complex (IPRC) in Mahendragiri, Tamil Nadu, ISRO said on Thursday. In a post on X, the space agency said, “Flight acceptance hot test of CE20 cryogenic engine earmarked for the C32 upper stage of upcoming LVM3 mission at uprated thrust conditions of 220kN is successfully carried out at ISRO Propulsion Complex, Mahendragiri on September 09, 2026.” ISRO also said the performance of the LOX Tank Pressurisation Module (LTPM), intended for the C32 stages of the Gaganyaan missions, was successfully demonstrated during the test. Advertisement The CE20 engine powers the upper cryogenic stage of the LVM3 launch vehicle. The space agency has been working to operate future LVM3 missions with an uprated C32 stage using the CE20 engine at 22-tonne thrust to enhance the vehicle’s payload capability. The latest test follows a sea-level hot test of the CE20 engine conducted in March at the Mahendragiri facility at the 22-tonne thrust level. The test was carried out using a Nozzle Protection System and a multi-element igniter. Advertisement The March test was aimed at qualifying the engine for sea-level testing at the higher thrust level. ISRO had said the engine and test facility performed as expected during the 165-second test. The CE20’s high-area-ratio nozzle makes sea-level testing particularly challenging because of its low exit pressure. ISRO has noted that flow separation inside the nozzle can cause severe vibrations and thermal stresses, potentially affecting the nozzle’s structural integrity. The latest successful flight acceptance test marks another step towards operationalising the uprated C32 stage for upcoming LVM3 missions. The development also comes shortly after ISRO successfully launched the Advanced Earth Observation Satellite-05 (EOS-05) aboard the GSLV-F17 from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota on September 5. ISRO Chairman V Narayanan had described the mission as a significant achievement, noting that the 2,367-kg satellite was successfully placed in its intended orbit. He said the satellite would become India’s first dedicated imaging satellite from geosynchronous orbit once operationalised. articles.title: ISRO successfully hot-tests CE20 engine at 220 kN thrust for upcoming LVM3 mission
articles.content: ISRO successfully hot-tests CE20 engine at 220 kN thrust for upcoming LVM3 mission Edited By: Anand P Last Updated: 10 September 2026, 01:41 PM IST Flight acceptance hot test of CE20 cryogenic engine earmarked for the C32 upper stage of upcoming LVM3 mission New Delhi: The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) has completed a flight acceptance hot test of its CE20 cryogenic engine at an uprated thrust level of 220 kN, a development aimed at increasing the payload capability of the LVM3 launch vehicle and supporting the Gaganyaan programme. The test was conducted on September 9 at the ISRO Propulsion Complex (IPRC) in Mahendragiri, Tamil Nadu, the space agency said on Thursday. Sharing details on X, ISRO said, “Flight acceptance hot test of CE20 cryogenic engine earmarked for the C32 upper stage of upcoming LVM3 mission at uprated thrust conditions of 220 kN was successfully carried out at ISRO Propulsion Complex, Mahendragiri on September 09, 2026.” During the test, ISRO also successfully demonstrated the performance of the LOX Tank Pressurisation Module (LTPM), which is intended for use in the C32 stages of the Gaganyaan missions. The CE20 is the engine that powers the upper cryogenic stage of the LVM3 launch vehicle. ISRO is working towards operating future LVM3 missions with an uprated C32 stage powered by the CE20 engine at a 22-tonne thrust level to increase the launch vehicle's payload capability. The latest test follows a sea-level hot test of the CE20 engine conducted at the Mahendragiri facility in March at the same 22-tonne thrust level. That test used a Nozzle Protection System and a multi-element igniter and was conducted to qualify the engine for sea-level testing at the higher thrust level. ISRO had said the engine and test facility performed as expected during the 165-second test. Sea-level testing of the CE20 presents a particular challenge because of its high-area-ratio nozzle and the resulting low exit pressure. ISRO has noted that flow separation within the nozzle can lead to severe vibrations and thermal stresses, potentially threatening the structural integrity of the nozzle. The successful flight acceptance hot test is another step towards operationalising the uprated C32 stage for future LVM3 missions. The development comes days after ISRO successfully launched the Advanced Earth Observation Satellite-05 (EOS-05) aboard the GSLV-F17 from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota on September 5. ISRO Chairman V Narayanan had termed the mission a significant achievement after the 2,367-kg satellite was successfully placed in its intended orbit. He said the satellite would become India's first dedicated imaging satellite from geosynchronous orbit once it is operationalised. (ANI) Published: 10 September 2026, 01:41 PM IST

articles.title: A Homegrown Art Lover's Guide To New Galleries & Museums In Kolkata
articles.content: Kolkata’s cultural landscape is evolving with new spaces that celebrate art, language, and heritage. From Shabdalok at the National Library, India’s first museum of linguistic diversity, to NGMA’s modern art hub in the Old Currency Building, the city now offers rich experiences that connect contemporary creativity with layered histories and marginalised communities. Kolkata’s cultural landscape has always been shaped by how its institutions, archives, and independent creative spaces spilled into the city’s public life. Now, a new generation of museums and galleries is adding a breath of fresh air into that well-trodden cultural map. From an immersive museum exploring India’s many languages to a new home for contemporary art, a space preserving the cultural heritage of Kolkata’s Chinese community, and a former colonial prison turned museum, these spaces offer different ways of looking at the city and its layered past. Here are five new and noteworthy museums and galleries to add to your Kolkata itinerary: The Shabdalok, or Museum of Word, located in Belvedere House on the National Library campus in Alipore, is India’s first museum dedicated to the country’s linguistic diversity and literary heritage . Its galleries explore the evolution of languages and scripts, the relationship between language and identity, and the country’s rich regional traditions of oral storytelling and performance. Address: Belvedere House, National Library campus, Alipore The National Gallery of Modern Art’s Kolkata campus is a cultural space dedicated to modern and contemporary Indian art . Housed in the Old Currency Building in Dalhousie Square, Kolkata’s historic centre, the space puts Indian creative practices in conversation with the country’s changing social, political, and cultural landscape. Address: Old Currency Building, Dalhousie Square The Cheenapara Heritage Gallery is India’s only heritage space dedicated to India’s small but significant Indian-Chinese community. Located in Tiretta Bazar, inside India’s oldest living Chinatown, the intimate museum and gallery archives the story of Kolkata’s Chinese community, shaped by colonial-era migration and subsequent assimilation, food culture, and trade. This is a natural entry point to the city’s Chinese heritage for those interested in Kolkata’s lesser-known histories. Address: 17, Blackburn Lane, Tiretta Bazar Once one of the most notorious prison complexes of the British Raj, the Alipore Central Jail was converted into the Alipore Museum in 2022, today, the museum houses an outpost of the Experimenter gallery and several permanent exhibitions archiving Kolkata’s colonial and political past through the architecture of incarceration, personal histories and the material traces of prison life. Follow @aliporemuseumkol on Instagram. Address: 17, Judges Court Road, Alipore Trace Gallery is Kolkata’s newest contemporary art gallery in South Kolkata, founded by Anissa Sonthalia. The gallery platforms multidisciplinary contemporary creative practices across art, design, and music. Follow @traceartgallery on Instagram. articles.title: First Indian Genome -Wide Study Reveals Genetic Links to Endometriosis
articles.content: Medi News Facebook Twitter Linkedin India’s first nationwide genome-wide study on endometriosis has identified genetic factors that may influence a woman’s risk of developing the condition. Researchers analysed genetic data from 2,523 women across 18 centres and identified 21 genetic regions linked to endometriosis. The strongest signal appeared on chromosome 13 near the SHISA2/LINC00415 region. Researchers also identified signals in known endometriosis-associated regions, including WNT4 and CDKN2B-AS1. Why the Study Matters Most previous genetic studies on endometriosis have focused on European and East Asian populations. Therefore, this research provides valuable genetic data from Indian women. As per The Economic Times, the findings could help researchers better understand the genetic basis of endometriosis and support future advances in diagnosis and treatment. Potential for Earlier Diagnosis Endometriosis can cause severe pelvic pain, painful periods and infertility, yet many women face delays in diagnosis. Understanding genetic risk could eventually help doctors identify women who are more susceptible to the condition. Also Read | A Remote-Controlled CAR-T Therapy for Cancer Treatment However, the researchers note that these findings are not yet ready for routine clinical testing. Larger studies will be needed before genetic screening can become part of standard healthcare. A Step Towards Precision Medicine The study provides an important foundation for future endometriosis research in India. In the long term, these findings could contribute to earlier diagnosis and more personalised treatment approaches.

articles.title: Travelxp Launches Marco, India's First Travel AI Agent - Marksmen Daily
articles.content: Travelxp becomes the first travel platform in India to launch an AI agent that can plan, pay for, and manage a trip on a traveler’s behalf Travelxp, India’s first content-led travel commerce platform, has launched Marco , an agentic AI trip concierge, the first of its kind from an Indian travel platform, at Global Fintech Fest 2026 in Mumbai. Marco can discover, plan, book and pay for a trip on a traveller’s behalf, within spending limits the preset by the traveller. The shift is already under way in some countries: Poke, a text-based AI assistant, exchanged over 100 million user messages in the three months before its acquisition by Cognition in July 2026; Instinct, a similar agent, raised a $250 million Series B at a $2.5 billion valuation, taking its total funding to roughly $350 million, within months of its 2026 launch, both used in part to handle travel bookings and logistics. No Indian travel platform has brought this model to travel specifically. Travelxp is the first to do so, launching Marco at Global Fintech Fest 2026 in Mumbai. What changes for travelers Today, booking a multi-part trip typically means comparing flights on one platform, hotels on another, arranging local transport separately, and manually tracking a budget across all of it. With Marco , a traveller sets a destination, a budget, and their preferences once. Marco then searches, books and pays across flights, hotels, transfers and activities directly, only returning to the traveller for approval when a decision falls outside the limits they’ve set. For a traveller, this means fewer steps and less manual coordination. Marco also stays active after booking. If a flight is delayed or prices shift, it can assess the impact on the rest of the itinerary and adjust connected bookings, hotel check-in, a transfer, an activity slot, without the traveller needing to open multiple apps or contact each provider separately. How the Payment Layer works The system is built on a new agentic payment infrastructure that lets Marco initiate and execute payments on its own, within permissions the traveller defines upfront: total budget, categories it can spend on, and any actions that require the traveller’s explicit approval before proceeding. This is the piece that has been missing from most AI travel tools to date, the ability for an agent to not just recommend, but to transact. A 2026 research from IMG found a gap among travellers who use AI for trip planning, 75% use it for recommendations, while only 13% use it to complete an actual booking. Because a single trip can involve payments to airlines, hotels, transfer operators and activity providers, all as separate transactions with separate merchants. Marco’s role is to treat the trip as one connected budget rather than a series of disconnected purchases, closing the gap between AI that suggests and AI that books. First in India, launched at Global Fintech Fest Travelxp is the first Indian travel platform to launch an end-to-end agentic payment experience, unveiled live at Global Fintech Fest...

articles.title: India's First Bullet Train to Be Inaugurated in 2027: Vaishnaw - Hindusthan Samachar English
articles.content: New Delhi, 09 September (H.S.): Union Information and Broadcasting and Railways Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said on Wednesday that the country’s first bullet train will be inaugurated in 2027. He said the indigenously manufactured bullet train is expected to begin track trials in May-June 2027, following which it will be inaugurated after the completion of testing. At a press conference convened to brief the media on the decisions taken by the Cabinet, Vaishnaw said the inauguration of the bullet train has been scheduled for 2027. Initially, there were plans to commence operations on an approximately 50-kilometre stretch between Surat and Bilimora, but the plan has now been expanded to cover the first section from Surat to Vapi, spanning around 100 kilometres, which is scheduled to be opened in 2027. The construction of this section is targeted for completion by December 2026. The minister said the construction of one coach of the bullet train being manufactured in India was completed last week. The coach will subsequently undergo pressure and climate-related tests, while other works, including interior fittings, will also be completed. The train is planned to be brought onto the tracks for testing by May-June next year. Following the completion of trials, the Prime Minister will inaugurate the service. It may be recalled that Vaishnaw had also said in Vadodara a day earlier that the country’s indigenously manufactured bullet train would be brought onto the tracks for testing in May-June 2027 and could be inaugurated two to four months after the trials. He had said that the first body frame of the train had been completed and sent for testing. The Mumbai-Ahmedabad High-Speed Rail Corridor has a total length of 508 kilometres. Work on the project is underway in Gujarat, Maharashtra and the Union Territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli. The proposed bullet train will have a maximum operating speed of 320 kilometres per hour.
